chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at what age a child is required to perform prayer, so he said: 'Between seven and six years.' I said: 'At what age is he required to fast?' He said: 'Between fifteen or fourteen, and if he fasts before that, let him be, for my son so-and-so fasted before that and I let him be.'
ai.seo_question: At what age do children become obligated to pray and fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the transitional ages for ritual obligations, specifying that prayer instruction begins between six and seven years, while fasting is introduced between fourteen and fifteen. The Imam’s personal example of allowing his son to fast before the age of obligation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on gradual habituation (*tadrij*) and parental encouragement over strict legal compulsion during the preparatory phase.
